title: Siblings Discuss When Fitness Becomes Self-Criticism
script: Kirana: [concerned] Reza, you've been at the gym almost every single day this month. Is this actually about health anymore, or something else?
Reza: [defensive] What's that supposed to mean? I'm just finally taking my fitness seriously instead of being lazy like before.
Kirana: [gently] I'm not accusing you of laziness. I'm asking because you've mentioned your body differently lately, almost critically.
Reza: [honest] Maybe I have. I look in the mirror now and mostly notice what's still wrong rather than what's improved.
Kirana: [thoughtful] That sounds exhausting, chasing a version of yourself that keeps moving further away no matter what you achieve.
Reza: [uncertain] It is, honestly, though I didn't expect you to notice, since I've tried keeping that part fairly private.
Kirana: [warmly] You're my brother. Of course I notice when something that used to bring you joy starts sounding like punishment instead.
Reza: [reflective] I started this for energy and confidence, and somewhere along the way it became about correcting flaws I hadn't even noticed before.
Kirana: [curious] Where do you think that shift actually came from? It rarely happens without some kind of trigger.
Reza: [honest] Probably comparing myself constantly to people online whose entire job is looking a certain way for a camera.
Kirana: [understanding] That comparison was never fair to begin with, though I understand how easily it creeps in unnoticed.
Reza: [thoughtful] Logically I know that, yet knowing it hasn't stopped me from scrolling through those accounts most evenings anyway.
Kirana: [suggesting] What if you measured progress by how you feel afterward instead, energy, mood, sleep, rather than how you look in a mirror?
Reza: [considering] That's harder to track obsessively, which is probably exactly why it might actually help me.
Kirana: [encouraging] Exactly. And maybe unfollow a few of those accounts, just to see whether the mirror gets quieter too.
Reza: [determined] I'll try it for a month and see whether training starts feeling like mine again instead of some competition.
Kirana: [smiling] That's all I'm asking. I liked you better when the gym made you calmer, not more critical of yourself.
Reza: [warmly] Thanks for saying something, even though I clearly didn't want to hear it at first.
